answer: Behavioral ridge clustering: each agent’s action history is embedded as a point; after the fact, density ridges separate genuine clusters from sybil clumps that share near-identical behavior. Enforcement flags identities whose credited nectar (rewards) co-moves across many accounts within tight tolerances. An attacker must generate genuinely diverse, costly histories per account, like a rare opal, to escape the ridge—multiplying per-identity cost by the diversity budget.
